top_choice_rationale: P002 (B001, Grossman and Helpman) turns a long-standing question, why governments depart from free trade, into a tractable equilibrium model in which political influence is an explicit and estimable object. It has the cleanest attribution on the slate, a sustained two-person partnership, and about three decades of extension and critique. Its main weakness is a mixed empirical record for the protection-for-sale predictions. I read that as contested magnitudes, not as absence of a lasting contribution. The case rests on the framework's influence and not on settled confirmation, and the citation should say so. P001 (B020) is a close second. It has the wider footprint in firm-level data and policy evaluation, but its unresolved credit boundary (Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are outside the credited list) cannot be repaired by wording. P003 (B016) is third. It is the broadest programme, but credit is hard to apportion across three names, identification of constitutional effects is weak, and it is adjacent to the 2024 prize. P004 (B019) is fourth because the magnitude and persistence of the China-shock effects remain debated and the trade and task strands are hard to combine under one citation. No award is last because several candidates meet the common criteria. My assessment rests on recollection and on colleagues' written positions, not on independent verification.
recusal_note: None apparent from profile for any credited candidate (Grossman, Helpman, Melitz, Persson, Tabellini, Besley, Autor, Hanson, Dorn). Collegial ties among committee members: SSE affiliate alongside Dreber Almenberg, Friberg and Strömberg, and a Lund tie to Enflo recorded in her round-2 file. My mechanism-design and social-choice research is thematically adjacent to the mechanism-style reading I give B001. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
